description: Two crossing movements, seeded arrivals and fixed-time signals. Vehicles accelerate, queue and discharge along links and connectors.

editorDeleteDemandWarning: Delete this object? Deleting a route also removes its vehicle inputs. Undo restores the whole change.
editorRouteSegments: Links and connectors in travel order
editorRouteHelp: Choose a starting link, then append connected links and connectors in travel order. Remove last to revise the path. On the canvas, the Routes tool draws the same route: click the start, then click each destination. A route covers every lane of the links it names.
editorRouteClickHelp: Route tool: click the start link, then click a destination. Enter or double-click stores the route, Backspace removes the last object, Esc cancels. The route covers every lane.
editorInputPlaceHelp: Vehicle inputs tool: click the link traffic enters on. The volume is the link total, split across its lanes.
editorInputCountsPlaceholder: Optional — paste one count per interval, e.g. a 15-minute count column
editorInputCountsHelp: Optional (intervals). Each count is the vehicles counted in one interval, starting at the start time above. When counts are given they replace the volume and end time above, which are then derived from them. Clear the box to go back to one volume.
EDIT_INVALID_COUNTS: A count could not be read. Enter one non-negative number per interval, separated by new lines, spaces, commas or semicolons.
editorDecisionHelp: Turning proportions (routingDecisions). Give each route leaving the same link its relative flow — counted turning volumes work as they are, since only the proportions matter. A flow of 0 leaves the route out. A vehicle input that uses this decision is split across its routes; the split is exact for random arrivals, but like every figure here it is not validated. Placed on a link, the decision acts on every vehicle without a route that reaches it, and a row may be a destination link instead of a route. Placed on the link where the traffic enters, it puts each destination's vehicles in the lanes that reach it, so the proportions hold exactly; placed further on, a vehicle can only take the destinations its lane reaches, because lane changing is not modelled yet. Paste each row's counted volumes per interval to let the proportions change over the run; outside the counted intervals the whole-period flow applies. The interval is chosen by when a vehicle enters the network, not when it reaches the decision. The counts are proportions only: they split the vehicle input's own volume, so their totals and intervals need not match the input's, and an interval with no turn counted uses the whole-period proportions.
editorInputShareHelp: Optional (laneShares). Weights the split across the lanes above instead of dividing equally. Left alone, or if the drawing has changed since it was set, the split stays equal.
editorRunReady: Author routes and inputs, then Run.
editorRunStatus: Revision %1 · seed %2 · %3 s · active %4 · pending %5 · completed %6 · mean delay %7 s · safety clamps %8
editorRunStatusNote: Mean trip delay counts source waiting and acceleration, for completed trips only. Safety clamps count the steps where the prototype car-following had to be bounded. Diagnostics, not HCM control delay or LOS.

editorGestureHelp: Ctrl + right-drag: create Link or Connector. Select (S): orange handles on either side add/remove lanes while the opposite edge stays fixed. Ctrl + click: add to selection. Ctrl + drag selected objects: duplicate. Delete: objects. Ctrl + Delete: vertex. Conflict areas (A): click an area to select it, click it again or press P to cycle its priority, drag a dashed waiting line along its lane.
EDIT_LANE_RANGE: The connector lane range must fit within both links (1–12 lanes).
EDIT_DISPLAY_VALUE: Use a valid level and a nonempty display type.
EDIT_NAME_LENGTH: A name is at most 200 characters.
EDIT_DISPLAY_CATALOG: Could not read the levels or display types in the data directory.
EDIT_DUPLICATE_LINKS: Select at least one link to duplicate. Internal connectors and heads are copied with their links.
EDIT_CONNECTOR_POSITION: Connector position must be a finite distance in metres between the start and the end of its link.
EDIT_CREATION_TARGET: No object was created. Draw a link with a nonzero length, or release the connector on a visible target link.
EDIT_SPLIT_ATTACHMENT: The split would cut through a connector attachment. Move the split at least 0.1 m away from that position.
EDIT_NO_PRIORITY_DEFAULTS: This network has a connector arriving inside a link body, which is a merge, and the gap time and headway that arbitrate it could not be read from the data directory. Drawing, saving and editing are supported; Run needs data/priority-rules/ to be present.
UNSUPPORTED_CONNECTOR_POSITION: This connector leaves a link body too close to the end of the lane, or to another connector on the same lane, to leave a section either side of it. Drawing, saving and editing are supported; move it at least 0.2 m clear to run it.
UNSUPPORTED_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY: This route's links and connectors do not join up for a single lane, so no vehicle can travel it. Drawing, saving and editing are supported; connect the objects it names, or name the connector between them, to run it.
WARN_CONNECTOR_ALIGNMENT: The Connector reaches a Link too steeply or against its direction. A full-width square mouth is shown where lane alignment is impossible. Reset the curve or move the intermediate points/attachments to approach in the direction of travel.
UNKNOWN_COMPOSITION: This vehicle input names a vehicle composition that is not in data/compositions/. Choose another composition or a single vehicle type; the input does not run until then.
INVALID_SHARE: The vehicle composition this input uses has no vehicle types, or a share that is not a positive number. Fix the composition file in data/compositions/.
UNKNOWN_ROUTING_DECISION: This vehicle input names a routing decision that does not exist. Choose a route or an existing routing decision.
ROUTING_DECISION_MIXED_ORIGIN: Every route in a routing decision must start on the same link, because the decision splits the traffic entering there. Remove the route that starts elsewhere or give it its own decision.
AMBIGUOUS_ROUTE_STEP: This route runs, but one lane of it was left out: between two links it names, that lane reaches the next link by two connectors, and the route does not say which. Run is not blocked; name the connector you mean in the route to include that lane.
TIGHT_CONNECTOR_RADIUS: This connector turns tighter than its own width, so no vehicle could follow it. The drawing is kept and Run is not blocked; widen the turn or move the attachments apart.
EDIT_COPY_TARGET: Place copied Connector endpoints or signal heads on existing lanes at the same level. No objects were copied. Select both parent Links to copy the whole connection.
EDIT_MOVE_TARGET: Select at least one Link or Connector to move. Signal heads move with their parent road.
editorLinkMarkings: Boundary markings in lane order (N+1; solid/dashed/none/double; blank = defaults)
EDIT_LINK_STATION: Choose a finite station strictly between the Link endpoints.
EDIT_REFERENCED_LINK: Cannot reverse a Link used by a Connector or a signal head. Remove those references first. A route does not block it: a route names the link, not its lanes.
EDIT_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD: This project contains a field this version does not support. See the problem path; opening was cancelled to avoid losing data.
INVALID_MARKING: Use solid, dashed, none or double for each marking.
WARN_SHORT_CONNECTOR: Connector is shorter than 5 m. Check the geometry; this advisory does not block Run or Save.
editorHistoryHelp: Double-click a state or press Enter to restore it. Up to 100 edits are kept for this session.
EDIT_HISTORY_REVISION: This history state is no longer available. Choose a state from the current list.
editorKeyboardHelp: Select (S): arrow keys move selected Links/Connectors by the grid interval (1 m with Snap off); Shift moves ten intervals. Ctrl+Shift+H opens History. Alt + left-drag rotates the selection; hold Shift for 15° steps. Ctrl+Shift+R enters an exact angle.
editorRotationHelp: Angle in degrees around the centre of the selected roads. Positive turns counter-clockwise; negative turns clockwise. Connectors that leave their parent roads are removed with their dependent routes and heads; Undo restores the whole edit.
EDIT_ROTATE_TARGET: Select at least one Link or Connector to rotate. Signal heads rotate with their parent road.
editorInputSplitHelp: The volume is the whole link's total. It is divided equally across the lanes the route reaches — an authoring convenience, not a lane-choice model: this engine has no lane changing, and none of these figures are validated.

editorInputLinkItem: No route — follow the network from %1
UNKNOWN_LINK: This names a link that does not exist. Choose an existing link.
ROUTELESS_CYCLE: Vehicles without a route entering here can drive round a loop and back onto a lane they already used, which the engine cannot run. Give them a route or a routing decision that leads out of the loop.
ROUTELESS_TOO_MANY_PATHS: Vehicles without a route entering here have more than 256 possible paths through the network. Place a routing decision to narrow where they go.
ROUTING_DECISION_DUPLICATE_LINK: Two routing decisions are placed on the same link. A vehicle reaching it can follow only one; merge them.
ROUTING_DECISION_UNREACHABLE: No lane of the decision's link can reach this destination along connectors. Choose a destination downstream of it.
ROUTING_DECISION_INTERVALS: This row needs one flow per interval of its routing decision. Re-enter the counts so every row covers the same intervals.
ROUTING_DECISION_LANE_UNSERVED: A lane of this decision's link reaches none of its destinations; with no lane changing, its vehicles carry on without a route. Add a destination that lane can reach if that is not intended.
ROUTING_DECISION_NEEDS_LINK: A destination is reached from where the decision is placed. Place the decision on a link, or use routes instead.
INPUT_TARGET_CONFLICT: This names both a route and a destination (or a link). Choose one.
editorHeadPlaceHelp: Click a lane where vehicles must stop: the signal head is the stop line. Drag a selected head to slide it along its lane.
editorTemplateFourPhase: 4 phases, one approach at a time: 4 signal groups, 120 s cycle
editorTimingDiagram: Timing over one cycle (seconds of the cycle)
editorTimingOk: Every signal group fits the cycle.
INVALID_SIGNAL_TIMING: A signal time does not fit the cycle: green start and green end must be different seconds of the cycle on the time step, and green plus amber must not exceed the cycle.
DUPLICATE_SIGNAL_GROUP: Each signal group needs its own whole number, 1 or more.
UNKNOWN_SIGNAL_GROUP: A signal head shows a signal group that does not exist. Choose another group for the head first.
EMPTY_SIGNAL_CONTROLLER: A signal controller needs at least one signal group.
EDIT_REFERENCED_CONTROLLER: Signal heads still show this controller's groups. Reassign or delete those heads first.
editorCrossingPairs: Creates one area for each of %1 crossing lane pairs.
editorRunProtection: Only conflict areas you author are protected. Other paths that cross on the drawing pass through each other in the run.
INVALID_MEASUREMENT_LINE: A queue counter line must name a signal head or waiting line, or give a point on a lane — exactly one of the two.
UNKNOWN_MEASUREMENT_REFERENCE: A queue counter line names a signal head or waiting line that does not exist.
CONFLICT_STOP_LINE_MISMATCH: A Stop/Yield control names an area that does not give way at the control's waiting line.
DUPLICATE_STOP_CONTROL: A waiting line or conflict area has more than one Stop/Yield control.
INVALID_STOP_CONTROL: A Stop/Yield control names no conflict area.
EDIT_UNDETERMINED_PRIORITY: Decide which side gives way before setting Stop or Yield.
CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_PAIR: Two conflict areas cover the same pair of paths.
CONFLICT_EXTENT_UNCOVERED: The conflict area's extent does not cover where the two lanes really overlap.
CONFLICT_GEOMETRY_UNSUPPORTED: These two lanes overlap in a way that cannot be measured (they cross twice, or a lane folds on a tight bend).
CONFLICT_GROUP_INCOMPLETE: A merge taken over from automatic priority does not order every pair of its paths.
CONFLICT_HOLD_CYCLE: These conflict areas can deadlock: vehicles holding one wait for vehicles holding another, in a loop.
CONFLICT_MERGE_TOPOLOGY: A merge area's two paths do not arrive at the same place.
CONFLICT_NO_OVERLAP: The two lanes of this crossing area do not overlap.
CONFLICT_PRIORITY_CYCLE: The priorities in this merge form a cycle, so nobody has priority.
CONFLICT_ROUTE_JOINS_INSIDE: A route enters the yielding side part way through, without passing the waiting line.
CONFLICT_ROUTE_STARTS_PAST_LINE: A route starts past the waiting line, so its vehicles never ask to enter.
CONFLICT_RULE_MISSING: This conflict area has a priority but no gapTime and headway.
CONFLICT_SINK_TOO_CLOSE: A route ends too close after the conflict area for the longest vehicle to clear it.
CONFLICT_UNDETERMINED: This conflict area's priority is undetermined.
CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED_PATH: A conflict area or waiting line names a lane or position that no longer exists.
CONFLICT_WAITING_LINE_AFTER_ENTRY: The waiting line is inside or after the conflict area.
CONFLICT_WAITING_LINE_BYPASSED: A route can reach the conflict area without passing its waiting line.
CONFLICT_WAITING_LINE_NOT_UPSTREAM: The waiting line is not upstream of its conflict area.
DUPLICATE_PRIORITY_RULE: A conflict area has more than one priority rule.
EDIT_ALREADY_EXPLICIT: This merge already has authored priority.
EDIT_NO_CROSSING: No lane of the two selected objects overlaps a lane of the other.
EDIT_NO_MERGE: There is no automatic merge here to take over or restore.
EDIT_REFERENCED: A conflict area still uses this waiting line.
EDIT_SAME_OBJECT: Select two different Links or Connectors.
EDIT_SPLIT_CONTROL: The split point falls inside a conflict area or on a waiting line.
INVALID_CONFLICT_EXTENT: A conflict area's entry must come before its exit.
INVALID_CONTROL_PATH: A control must name either one Link lane or one Connector lane pair.
INVALID_PRIORITY_RULE: gapTime and headway must be greater than zero.
UNKNOWN_CONFLICT_AREA: A priority rule names a conflict area that does not exist.
UNKNOWN_CONTROL_OWNER: A control names a Link or Connector that does not exist.
UNKNOWN_WAITING_LINE: A conflict area names a waiting line that does not exist.
